## Microservice CI/CD Pipeline Design

Scope, per the working overview:

1. **Phase 0 (prerequisite, lives in `platform-engineering-project`):** the infra CI/CD pipelines for `staging` and `shared` already exist and must be confirmed working before this repo's CD pipeline has anywhere to deploy to.
2. **Phase 1:** CI pipeline for the 5 microservices — build, container image build, Trivy container scan, Semgrep SAST (DAST if time permits).
3. **Phase 2:** CD pipeline — build, scan (Trivy + Semgrep), push to Artifact Registry, hand off to ArgoCD Image Updater to roll the image out.

This version is corrected against the actual state of both repos (verified by reading the code directly, not assumed) — see **Corrections from the first draft** and **Cross-repo prerequisites** below before implementing.

---

### Corrections from the first draft

The first draft of this plan referenced patterns/components as "already existing" that turned out to live in — or be missing entirely from — `platform-engineering-project`. Verified facts:

| Assumption | Reality |
|---|---|
| `.github/actions/netbird-connect/action.yaml` "already exists" (in this repo) | Exists in **`platform-engineering-project`**, not here. It VPN-connects a runner into the private mesh to reach GSM secrets / private GKE. **Not needed for this repo's pipelines** — CI needs no GCP access at all, and CD only needs public GCP APIs (WIF auth + `gcloud`/Artifact Registry push), same as `terraform-workflow-template.yaml`'s non-VPN steps. Don't wire it in unless a future step needs the private network. |
| `staging-infra.yml` as an existing "same pattern" precedent | The actual file is `staging-infra.yaml` (note: `.yaml`, not `.yml`) in `platform-engineering-project`. It does use `dorny/paths-filter` in a `detect` job feeding conditional downstream jobs — that part of the plan is validated, just cite the real filename/repo. |
| Node 20 runtime | products, search, and store-ui all pin **Node 18** (Dockerfile base images + the existing `node.js.yml` matrix). Use `actions/setup-node` with Node 18 to match what's actually built and shipped, not 20. |
| `npm test --if-present` will safely skip missing tests | products and search both **have** a `test` script — it's a placeholder (`echo "Error: no test specified" && exit 1`) that exits non-zero. `--if-present` only skips an *absent* script, so CI will hard-fail on both today. See **Open decisions** below. |
| ArgoCD Image Updater "then polls Artifact Registry... no extra step needed" | **Not installed.** `terraform/kubernetes/argocd/charts.tf` in `platform-engineering-project` installs `argo-cd` via Helm with no Image Updater subchart or values anywhere in the repo. Today, image versions are static Terraform variables (`users_microservice_image_tag`, `store_ui_image_tag`, both defaulting to `"v1"`) baked into the ArgoCD `Application` Helm values by Terraform (`terraform/kubernetes/argocd-apps/locals.tf:8-9`) — "bump here to roll out a new version" per the variable's own description. Installing and wiring Image Updater is real, separate infra work in `platform-engineering-project` — see prerequisites. |
| Artifact Registry project/region | Region is consistently `us-central1` and the repo name is consistently `images` (`terraform/envs/staging/artifact-registry` in `platform-engineering-project`, repositories map key `images`). The service project ID is **not a fixed string** — it's `pe-staging-project-<random-hex>`, generated by `terraform/modules/projects` (`random_id`). The differing project IDs found across the 5 microservice READMEs (`pe-staging-project-131b` vs `pe-staging-project-a422`) are stale docs from before the project was recreated (see "Switched basic project and domains to new organization set up" in `platform-engineering-project` history) — don't hardcode either. Resolve the live value the same way the infra workflows do: GitHub Actions variable `vars.TF_PROJECT`. |
| Only `users` and `store-ui` are ArgoCD-managed | Confirmed — `terraform/kubernetes/argocd-apps/applications.tf` in `platform-engineering-project` has **no** `Application` resource for `cart`, `products`, or `search`. Those three only exist as local Kustomize manifests in this repo (`infra/k8s/apps/base/{cart,products,search}`), which is a Minikube-only path disconnected from GKE/ArgoCD entirely. Pushing a scanned image to Artifact Registry for these three does nothing on the platform until Applications are created for them (same `helm/custom-charts/microservice` chart pattern as users/store-ui). This is real, separate infra work — see prerequisites. |
| Branch model: CI on PR to `staging`/`main`, CD on push to `staging`/`main` | This repo only has a `master` branch (confirmed via `git branch -a` — no `staging`/`main`). Per the platform's own accomplishments log, the `production/` env is also not yet implemented on the infra side. Design CI on PR→`master`, CD on push→`master`→`staging` environment only, for now. A `production` path can mirror `platform-engineering-project`'s branch model once that side actually exists. |

### Reference patterns adopted from `platform-engineering-project` (validated)

These patterns are real, live, and should be mirrored as-is:

- **WIF auth block**, from `terraform-workflow-template.yaml`:
  ```yaml
  - uses: google-github-actions/auth@v2
    with:
      service_account: ${{ vars.CICD_SA_EMAIL }}
      workload_identity_provider: ${{ vars.WIF_PROVIDER }}
  ```
- **`workflow_call` reusable-template + caller** split, with a `detect` job running `dorny/paths-filter@v3` upfront and downstream jobs gated by `if: needs.detect.outputs.<x> == 'true'`, exactly as in `staging-infra.yaml` / `production-infra.yaml`.
- **`environment: ${{ inputs.github-environment }}`** set on the reusable template's job (not the caller) — "so env-scoped vars resolve correctly," per the existing comment convention.
- GitHub environments are named `staging` / `production` (`shared` also exists for the one-off shared-infra apply) — reuse these same environment names and their existing `CICD_SA_EMAIL` / `WIF_PROVIDER` environment variables rather than creating microservices-specific ones, since it's the same GCP projects and the same CI/CD SA.

### Verified per-service facts

| Service | Dir | Build file | Test status | Runtime pinned | Dockerfile | Non-root |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| cart | `cart-cna-microservice/` | `build.gradle` | Real JUnit test (`CartRedisOperationsTest`) | Java 17 | multi-stage, `gradle:7.5-jdk17-alpine` → `eclipse-temurin:17-jre-alpine` | yes (`spring:spring`) |
| products | `products-cna-microservice/` | `package.json` | Placeholder, `exit 1`, no test files | Node 18 | single-stage, `node:18-alpine` | **no** |
| search | `search-cna-microservice/` | `package.json` | Placeholder, `exit 1`, no test files | Node 18 | single-stage, `node:18-alpine` | **no** |
| users | `users-cna-microservice/` | `Pipfile`/`Pipfile.lock` | No test files, no pytest dep | Python 3.11 (Dockerfile) | single-stage w/ build-dep cleanup, `python:3.11-alpine` | yes (`app:app`) |
| store-ui | `store-ui/` | `package.json` | Real CRA/Jest test (`Home.test.tsx`) | Node 18 | multi-stage, `node:18-alpine3.16` → `nginx:1.21.6-alpine` | **no** |

All 5 Dockerfiles live at `<service-dir>/Dockerfile` with `COPY` paths relative to that directory — `context: inputs.working-directory`, `file: ./Dockerfile` needs no per-service override.

---

### Repo structure

```
.github/
  workflows/
    ci-pipeline.yml           ← reusable CI template (workflow_call)
    cd-pipeline.yml           ← reusable CD template (workflow_call)
    microservices-ci.yml      ← CI caller: detects changes, calls CI template per service
    microservices-cd.yml      ← CD caller: detects changes, calls CD template per service
```

No `.github/actions/` needed in this repo for now (see netbird-connect correction above).

---

### Change detection strategy

Both caller workflows use `dorny/paths-filter@v3` in a `detect` job upfront, matching `platform-engineering-project`'s pattern:

```
cart      → cart-cna-microservice/**
products  → products-cna-microservice/**
search    → search-cna-microservice/**
users     → users-cna-microservice/**
store-ui  → store-ui/**
```

Downstream jobs run conditionally: `if: needs.detect.outputs.cart == 'true'`, etc.

---

### CI reusable template (`ci-pipeline.yml`)

**Trigger:** `workflow_call`

**Inputs:**

| Input | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `service-name` | string | e.g. `cart`, `products` |
| `working-directory` | string | e.g. `cart-cna-microservice` |
| `dockerfile-path` | string | default `./Dockerfile` |

No `github-environment` input needed here — CI needs no GCP auth, so it needs no GitHub environment gating either.

**Steps:**

```
1. Checkout
      └── actions/checkout@v4

2. Detect runtime (for build step)
      └── Inline script: build.gradle → Java, package.json → Node, Pipfile → Python
          (unambiguous per service — verified no conflicting build files exist)

3. Set up runtime
      └── Conditional:
          Java   → actions/setup-java (temurin, Java 17)
          Node   → actions/setup-node (Node 18 — matches Dockerfiles, NOT 20)
          Python → actions/setup-python (3.11)

4. Build / compile
      └── Conditional:
          Java   → ./gradlew build -x test
          Node   → npm ci   (store-ui additionally: npm run build)
          Python → pipenv install --deploy

5. Unit tests
      └── Conditional:
          Java   → ./gradlew test                 (real tests: cart)
          Node   → npm test --if-present            (real tests: store-ui;
                    products & search WILL fail here today — see Open Decisions)
          Python → pytest (only if a tests/ dir exists — currently a no-op for users)

6. Semgrep SAST scan
      └── semgrep/semgrep-action
          config: auto (OSS ruleset, no token needed)
          working-directory: inputs.working-directory
          Fail on: error-level findings

7. Build container image (no push, for Trivy scan target)
      └── docker/build-push-action
          push: false
          tags: ${{ inputs.service-name }}:ci-scan
          context: inputs.working-directory
          file: inputs.dockerfile-path
          load: true

8. Trivy container scan
      └── aquasecurity/trivy-action
          image-ref: ${{ inputs.service-name }}:ci-scan
          format: table
          exit-code: 1
          severity: CRITICAL,HIGH
          ignore-unfixed: true
```

**No GCP auth in CI** — no push, no secrets pulled. Fast and credential-free, same rationale as the original draft.

**DAST (if time permits):** add as a separate optional job in the caller, not the reusable CI template — DAST needs a *running* instance (e.g. OWASP ZAP baseline scan against a docker-compose'd service + its datastore), which is meaningfully heavier and per-service-shaped (products needs Mongo up, cart needs Redis up, users needs Postgres/SQLite up). Treat as a stretch job gated by a workflow_dispatch input rather than blocking every PR.

---

### CD reusable template (`cd-pipeline.yml`)

**Trigger:** `workflow_call`

**Inputs:**

| Input | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `service-name` | string | e.g. `cart` |
| `working-directory` | string | e.g. `cart-cna-microservice` |
| `dockerfile-path` | string | default `./Dockerfile` |
| `github-environment` | string | `staging` (only environment that currently exists — see corrections) |
| `artifact-registry-region` | string | default `us-central1` |
| `artifact-registry-repo` | string | default `images` |

**Secrets:** `inherit`

Project ID is **not** an input — resolve it the same way the infra pipelines do, from `vars.TF_PROJECT` inside the `github-environment` context set on the job (matches `staging-infra.yaml`'s `gcp-project-id: ${{ vars.TF_PROJECT }}`).

**GitHub environment:** set on the job inside the template (`environment: ${{ inputs.github-environment }}`) — same reasoning as the infra templates, so env-scoped vars resolve correctly.

**Steps:**

```
1. Checkout
      └── actions/checkout@v4

2. Authenticate to GCP via WIF
      └── google-github-actions/auth@v2
          workload_identity_provider: vars.WIF_PROVIDER
          service_account: vars.CICD_SA_EMAIL

3. Set up runtime (same conditional logic as CI template — Node 18/Java 17/Python 3.11)

4. Build / compile (same as CI template)

5. Semgrep SAST scan (same as CI template — fail on error-level findings)

6. Configure Docker auth for Artifact Registry
      └── gcloud auth configure-docker ${artifact-registry-region}-docker.pkg.dev

7. Compute image tag
      └── Inline script:
          TAG="${{ github.sha }}"
          FULL_IMAGE="${artifact-registry-region}-docker.pkg.dev/${{ vars.TF_PROJECT }}/${artifact-registry-repo}/${service-name}:${TAG}"
          echo "image=$FULL_IMAGE" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

8. Build and push container image
      └── docker/build-push-action
          push: true
          tags: steps.tag.outputs.image
          context: inputs.working-directory
          file: inputs.dockerfile-path

9. Trivy container scan (post-push, scan the pushed image)
      └── aquasecurity/trivy-action
          image-ref: steps.tag.outputs.image
          format: sarif
          output: trivy-results.sarif
          severity: CRITICAL,HIGH
          ignore-unfixed: true

10. Upload Trivy SARIF to GitHub Security tab
       └── github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v3
           sarif_file: trivy-results.sarif

11. Summary
       └── echo image tag to job summary
```

**This pipeline's job ends at step 11.** It does not call `kubectl`/`argocd` and does not bump any Terraform variable itself — see the prerequisite below for what has to exist on the platform side before pushing an image here actually results in a rollout.

---

### CI caller (`microservices-ci.yml`)

**Trigger:** `pull_request` targeting `master`

```
detect:
  uses: dorny/paths-filter@v3
  outputs: cart, products, search, users, store-ui

ci-cart:
  if: needs.detect.outputs.cart == 'true'
  uses: ./.github/workflows/ci-pipeline.yml
  with:
    service-name: cart
    working-directory: cart-cna-microservice
  secrets: inherit

ci-products: ... (products-cna-microservice)
ci-search:   ... (search-cna-microservice)
ci-users:    ... (users-cna-microservice)
ci-store-ui: ... (store-ui)
```

### CD caller (`microservices-cd.yml`)

**Trigger:** `push` to `master` (paths: any service directory)

```
detect:
  uses: dorny/paths-filter@v3
  outputs: cart, products, search, users, store-ui

cd-cart:
  if: needs.detect.outputs.cart == 'true'
  uses: ./.github/workflows/cd-pipeline.yml
  with:
    service-name: cart
    working-directory: cart-cna-microservice
    github-environment: staging
  secrets: inherit

cd-products: ... / cd-search: ... / cd-users: ... / cd-store-ui: ...
```

No `main`/production branch or environment logic for now — add it once a `production` GKE environment and branch actually exist on the infra side (currently `terraform/envs/production/` is empty in `platform-engineering-project`).

---

### Cross-repo prerequisites (real gaps — must be resolved in `platform-engineering-project`, not here)

These block the CD pipeline from doing anything useful beyond "push a scanned image to a registry nothing reads from":

1. **Install & configure ArgoCD Image Updater.** Not present today (`terraform/kubernetes/argocd/charts.tf` has no Image Updater values). Needs: the Image Updater Helm component added alongside the existing `argo-cd` release, registry credentials for it to read the `images` Artifact Registry repo, and `argocd-image-updater.argoproj.io/image-list` (+ write-back method) annotations added to the `users` and `store-ui` `Application` resources in `terraform/kubernetes/argocd-apps/applications.tf`.
2. **Create ArgoCD `Application` resources for `cart`, `products`, `search`.** None exist. They'd follow the exact same pattern as `users`/`store-ui` in `applications.tf` (same `helm/custom-charts/microservice` chart, own namespace, own `*_image_tag` variable). Until this exists, images pushed by this repo's CD pipeline for these 3 services have no consumer.
3. **Confirm the CI/CD SA has `artifactregistry.writer`** on the `images` repo. `terraform/modules/iam_policies` currently only documents `artifactregistry.admin` for `tf-platform` (repo management) and `artifactregistry.reader` for GKE nodes (`terraform/modules/gke/iam.tf:35`) — no writer role is documented for whatever SA `vars.CICD_SA_EMAIL` actually resolves to. Verify/grant before wiring up step 8 of the CD template.
4. **Decide the write-back strategy for Image Updater**, since today the image tag is a Terraform variable, not something Image Updater has ever touched: either (a) let Image Updater write back directly to the `Application`'s Helm parameter (`argocd-image-updater.argoproj.io/write-back-method: argocd`), which will drift from the Terraform-declared default and needs to be an accepted trade-off, or (b) keep Terraform as the source of truth and have the CD pipeline instead bump `users_microservice_image_tag`/`store_ui_image_tag` (and new per-service equivalents) via a `terragrunt apply` in `platform-engineering-project`, skipping Image Updater entirely. (a) is what "push image → ArgoCD auto-updates" implies and is closer to the target flow described; (b) is more consistent with how this platform manages everything else (Terraform-declared, no config drift). Worth a decision before building step 2 above.

---

### Open decisions still needed

- **products/search test placeholder:** `"test": "echo \"Error: no test specified\" && exit 1"` will hard-fail CI on every run for these two services today. Options: (a) write minimal real tests before turning CI on for these services, (b) change the placeholder to `exit 0` as an explicit "no tests yet" marker (tracked as tech debt, not silently hidden in the pipeline), or (c) skip the test step for these two specifically via a per-service input. Recommend (a) or (b) over a pipeline-side workaround.
- **DAST scope:** confirm target tool (OWASP ZAP baseline is the natural fit here) and which service(s) get it first if not all five, given the per-service datastore dependency noted above.
- **Semgrep:** OSS `auto` config (no token) vs. a Semgrep Cloud token, if available.
- **Non-root Dockerfiles:** products, search, and store-ui containers run as root today (no `USER` directive) — separate from CI/CD, but Trivy/DAST findings will likely flag this; worth deciding whether to fix these 3 Dockerfiles as part of this initiative or file as a follow-up.
